findings.title: Missing class-constructor guard in Maglev feedback-cell call reduction
findings.message: In `BuildCallWithFeedback`, when the feedback target is a `FeedbackCell` (rather than a direct `JSFunction`), Maglev retrieves the `SharedFunctionInfo` and—if it is present—immediately proceeds to emit an inlined call via `TryBuildCallKnownJSFunction` without first checking whether the callee is a class constructor. Class constructors are non-callable: invoking one without `new` must throw a `TypeError`. Because the guard is absent, Maglev-optimized code silently executes the class body as if it were an ordinary function call, producing an incorrect result (no exception is thrown) instead of the spec-required `TypeError`. The fix adds `if (IsClassConstructor(shared->kind())) return BuildCallRuntime(Runtime::kThrowConstructorNonCallableError, {target_node});` before any inlining proceeds.

ground_truth.root_cause: The code path added in commit a0e2148 for reducing calls via FeedbackCell shared-function-info only checks `shared.has_value()` before inlining, but omits the `IsClassConstructor(shared->kind())` guard that the rest of the call-reduction infrastructure applies when handling class constructors. The one-day gap between the introducing commit (May 26) and the fix (May 27) reflects rapid identification during fuzz/correctness testing.
